Boris Nadezhdin posted a video standing in front of the Eiffel Tower in Paris. He said: "Hi everyone. I have some good news. I'm alive and free. Unfortunately, I'm not in Russia at the moment." Nadezhdin, 63, came to prominence two years ago when he tried to stand for the presidency on an anti-war platform, but was barred because electoral authorities ruled signatures he had submitted were flawed. Image: Planet Labs Advertisement For years, Khasan was little more than a very remote place on the edge of Russia . Less than 500 people live in the village in the country's far east, more than 5,600 miles (9,012 kilometers) from Moscow.
